note.explanation: Use computers thoughtfully: protect your information, choose compatible hardware and software, respect other people’s rights, and check that online information is reliable.
examples: Use a strong, unique password and enable two-factor authentication.
Check who can see your social media posts before sharing them.
note.checkAnswer: Use strong, unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication.
note.simple: Stay safe online, respect other people’s work and privacy, and think carefully before you click or share.
note.checkQuestion: Name two ways to help keep an online account secure.
note.title: Responsible Computer Usage
steps: Choose hardware and software that fit your needs and work together.
Keep devices and software updated, and use antivirus software.
Protect accounts with strong, unique passwords and 2FA.
Avoid suspicious links, downloads, messages, and sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi.
Use privacy settings and share personal information carefully.
Respect intellectual property and check online sources before trusting them.
note.answer: Use computers safely and responsibly by protecting your data, making careful choices, respecting privacy and intellectual property, and checking information before relying on it.

options: To ensure we can use them more frequently
To protect our personal information and make wise choices about hardware and software
To make the computer run faster
To avoid paying for software
mcqs.stem: Q11.1. Why is it important to use computers safely and responsibly?
rationales: Using a computer more often is not the main purpose of safe, responsible use.
This is correct because responsible use protects personal information and supports wise choices.
Safe use does not necessarily make a computer run faster.
Avoiding payment for software is not responsible use and may involve piracy.

options: Choosing the most expensive hardware
Sharing your passwords with friends
Being cautious about what you share online and protecting yourself and others
Ignoring software updates
mcqs.stem: Q11.2. What does "responsible computer usage" include?
rationales: The most expensive hardware is not automatically the best or most responsible choice.
Sharing passwords can put accounts at risk.
This is correct because responsible use includes careful sharing and protecting people online.
Ignoring updates can leave software less secure.

options: The color of the hardware
The system requirements on software packages and match them with your computer's specifications
The price of the hardware
The brand of the hardware
mcqs.stem: Q11.3. What should you check to ensure hardware and software compatibility?
rationales: Color does not determine whether hardware and software work together.
This is correct because system requirements should be matched to the computer’s specifications.
Price alone does not show compatibility.
A brand name alone does not show compatibility.

options: To make your accounts easy to hack
To help others guess your password
To make it harder for someone to guess your password and access your accounts
To avoid installing software updates
mcqs.stem: Q11.4. Why is it important to use strong, unique passwords?
rationales: Strong, unique passwords help prevent hacking rather than make it easier.
A password should not be made easy for other people to guess.
This is correct because strong, unique passwords make unauthorized access harder.
Passwords do not remove the need for software updates.

options: They might contain helpful software
They might contain malware that can harm your device or steal your information
They are usually cheaper
They help your device run faster
mcqs.stem: Q11.5. What is one reason to avoid clicking on unknown links or downloading files from untrusted sources?
rationales: Unknown links and downloads should not be assumed to contain helpful software.
This is correct because they may contain malware that harms devices or steals information.
Being cheaper is not a reason to trust an unknown download.
Untrusted links are not a safe way to speed up a device.

options: It makes your password easier to guess
It adds an extra layer of security by requiring a second form of verification
It removes the need for a password
It reduces the need for software updates
mcqs.stem: Q11.6. What does Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) do?
rationales: 2FA is meant to strengthen security, not make a password easier to guess.
This is correct because 2FA requires a second form of verification.
2FA adds security and does not necessarily remove the password.
2FA does not replace software updates.

options: Public Wi-Fi is usually faster
Public Wi-Fi networks are often less secure
Public Wi-Fi is free
Public Wi-Fi always provides encryption
mcqs.stem: Q11.7. Why should you be cautious when using public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions?
rationales: Speed does not establish that a network is safe for sensitive transactions.
This is correct because public Wi-Fi networks are often less secure.
Free access does not guarantee security.
Public Wi-Fi does not always provide encryption.

options: Sharing personal information like your home address
Posting photos without considering privacy settings
Being respectful and avoiding sharing sensitive information publicly
Ignoring privacy settings
mcqs.stem: Q11.8. What is an important aspect of responsible use of social media?
rationales: Sharing a home address publicly can put privacy and safety at risk.
Posting without considering privacy settings can expose information.
This is correct because respectful use includes avoiding public disclosure of sensitive information.
Ignoring privacy settings can make information visible to unintended people.

options: Provide the information requested
Forward the email to your friends
Ignore or delete the email
Open the email and click on any links
mcqs.stem: Q11.9. What should you do if you receive an email from an unknown sender asking for personal information?
rationales: Providing personal information to an unknown sender is unsafe.
Forwarding it may spread a scam to others.
This is correct because ignoring or deleting the email avoids responding to a suspicious request.
Opening links may expose you to scams or harmful content.

options: To update your contact information
To look for unusual activity and ensure your accounts are secure
To check the number of friends you have
To download new applications
mcqs.stem: Q11.10. Why is it important to regularly review your account activity?
rationales: Updating contact information may be useful, but it is not the main purpose of reviewing account activity.
This is correct because unusual activity may indicate a security problem.
The number of friends does not show whether an account is secure.
Downloading applications is unrelated to reviewing account activity.

options: To make your posts public
To control who can see your information and interact with you online
To increase the number of followers
To automatically share your information
mcqs.stem: Q11.11. What is the purpose of privacy settings on digital platforms?
rationales: Privacy settings can restrict access rather than make all posts public.
This is correct because privacy settings help control visibility and interaction.
Privacy settings are not designed to increase followers.
They should help control sharing, not automatically share information.

options: Use the same password for all accounts
Share your passwords with friends
Use strong, unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication
Avoid using any security measures
mcqs.stem: Q11.12. What should you do to ensure data security?
rationales: Reusing one password means one exposed password can put several accounts at risk.
Sharing passwords can weaken account security.
This is correct because strong, unique passwords and 2FA strengthen protection.
Avoiding security measures leaves data less protected.

options: Using data in any way you like
Transparency, respect for privacy, and accountability in data usage
Collecting as much data as possible
Ignoring data security
mcqs.stem: Q11.13. What is a key aspect of data ethics?
rationales: Ethical data use is not unrestricted; it must respect people and their information.
This is correct because transparency, privacy, and accountability are key data ethics principles.
Collecting as much data as possible can disregard privacy and necessity.
Ignoring security is not ethical handling of data.

Buying from an official source is a lawful way to obtain software.
Updating software regularly is not software piracy.

rationales: The number of advertisements does not establish that information is reliable.
This is correct because comparison with reputable sources and checking the author’s credentials help verify credibility.
An attractive design does not prove that information is accurate.
Popularity alone does not prove that information is reliable.

written.text: Q11.1. What is the importance of using computers safely and responsibly?
written.finalAnswer: It protects personal information, helps prevent harm, and supports wise, responsible choices when using computers.

rubric.why: Protection of personal information is a central reason for safe use.
rubric.how: State that safe use helps protect personal information.

rubric.why: The answer should also explain responsible or careful use.
rubric.description: Give another benefit of responsible use.
rubric.how: Mention preventing harm or making wise choices.

modelAnswer: Using computers safely and responsibly protects personal information.
It helps prevent harm and supports wise choices when using computers.

written.text: Q11.2. How does choosing the right hardware and software affect your computer usage?
written.finalAnswer: The right hardware and software improve safety, efficiency, and compatibility, helping the computer perform the tasks you need.

rubric.why: Compatible components and programs can work together properly.
rubric.how: State that suitable choices help hardware and software work together.

rubric.why: Suitable choices also affect safe and effective use.
rubric.description: Give another effect of choosing suitable equipment and software.
rubric.how: Mention efficiency, safety, or performing needed tasks.

modelAnswer: Choosing suitable hardware and software helps them work together and perform the tasks you need.
It can improve compatibility, safety, and efficiency.

written.text: Q11.3. Why is it important to use antivirus software on your computer?
written.finalAnswer: Antivirus software helps detect, prevent, and remove malware that could damage the computer or steal information.

rubric.why: The answer must identify antivirus software’s role against malware.
rubric.how: Mention detecting, preventing, or removing malware.

rubric.why: The answer should connect malware protection to a benefit.
rubric.how: Mention protecting the device or information from harm or theft.

modelAnswer: Antivirus software helps detect, prevent, and remove malware.
This helps protect the computer from damage and personal information from theft.

written.text: Q11.4. What are some examples of good practices when selecting hardware and software?
written.finalAnswer: Check that products meet your needs, compare system requirements with your computer’s specifications, and use trusted sources.

rubric.why: Checking requirements helps ensure that the products will work together.
rubric.how: Match software requirements with computer specifications.

rubric.why: Good selection also involves suitability and trustworthy providers.
rubric.how: Mention choosing for your needs or using a trusted source.

modelAnswer: Check that the hardware and software meet your needs and come from trusted sources.
Compare software system requirements with your computer’s specifications to ensure compatibility.

written.text: Q11.5. How can choosing compatible hardware and software enhance your computer experience?
written.finalAnswer: Compatible hardware and software work together properly, improving performance and avoiding errors or problems.

rubric.why: Compatibility is the main idea asked about.
rubric.how: State that the components or programs work together.

rubric.why: The answer should give a practical improvement.
rubric.how: Mention improved performance or fewer errors and problems.

modelAnswer: Compatible hardware and software work together properly.
This can improve performance and avoid errors or other problems.

written.text: Q11.6. Why should you create strong, unique passwords for your accounts?
written.finalAnswer: Strong, unique passwords are harder to guess and help prevent unauthorized access to accounts.

rubric.why: Strong passwords reduce the chance of being guessed.
rubric.description: Explain why a password should be strong.
rubric.how: Say that it is harder to guess.

rubric.why: Unique passwords limit risk across accounts and protect access.
rubric.description: Explain the benefit of uniqueness or account protection.
rubric.how: Mention unique passwords or preventing unauthorized access.

modelAnswer: Strong passwords are harder for someone to guess.
Unique passwords help prevent unauthorized access to your accounts.

written.text: Q11.7. What is the purpose of regular software updates?
written.finalAnswer: Regular software updates fix problems, improve software, and help protect devices against security threats.

rubric.why: Updates are important for reducing security risks.
rubric.how: Explain that updates help protect against security threats.

rubric.why: Updates may also correct faults or improve software.
rubric.how: State that updates fix problems or improve software.

modelAnswer: Regular updates can fix problems and improve software.
They also help protect devices against security threats.

written.text: Q11.8. How can you protect yourself from harmful links and downloads?
written.finalAnswer: Avoid unknown links and downloads from untrusted sources, and check messages and files before opening them.

rubric.why: Avoiding untrusted links and files reduces exposure to harm.
rubric.how: Mention avoiding unknown links or untrusted downloads.

rubric.why: Careful checking helps identify potentially harmful content.
rubric.how: Say to verify messages or files before opening them.

modelAnswer: Do not click unknown links or download files from untrusted sources.
Check messages and files before opening them because they may contain malware.

written.text: Q11.9. What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), and why is it useful?
written.finalAnswer: 2FA requires a second form of verification as well as a password, adding an extra layer of account security.

rubric.why: The answer must describe what 2FA requires.
rubric.how: State that it requires a second form of verification.

rubric.why: The answer should explain its value.
rubric.how: Mention that it adds protection or makes unauthorized access harder.

modelAnswer: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) requires a second form of verification in addition to a password.
It adds an extra layer of security to help protect an account.

written.text: Q11.10. Why is it a good idea to avoid using public Wi-Fi for sensitive transactions?
written.finalAnswer: Public Wi-Fi networks are often less secure, so sensitive information may be exposed or intercepted.

rubric.why: The reason is the security risk of public Wi-Fi.
rubric.description: Identify the risk of public Wi-Fi.
rubric.how: State that public Wi-Fi is often less secure.

rubric.why: The answer should explain the possible consequence.
rubric.description: Explain what may happen to information.
rubric.how: Mention exposure or interception of sensitive information.

modelAnswer: Public Wi-Fi networks are often less secure.
Sensitive information used in a transaction could be exposed or intercepted.

written.text: Q11.11. How can you verify if an email or message is a scam?
written.finalAnswer: Check the sender and message for suspicious requests, links, or attachments, and verify claims through a trusted source before responding.

rubric.why: Scam signs should be identified before acting.
rubric.how: Check the sender, request, links, or attachments for suspicious features.

rubric.why: Verification or refusing risky requests reduces harm.
rubric.how: Verify independently or do not provide personal information.

modelAnswer: Check whether the sender, request, links, or attachments look suspicious.
Verify the message through a trusted source before responding or sharing information.

written.text: Q11.12. Why is it important to be careful about what you share on social media?
written.finalAnswer: Careful sharing protects your privacy and safety because public posts may reveal sensitive personal information.

rubric.why: The answer should identify what careful sharing protects.
rubric.how: Mention privacy, safety, or personal information.

rubric.why: The answer should explain the risk of oversharing.
rubric.description: Explain why public sharing can be risky.
rubric.how: Mention that sensitive information may be exposed or misused.

modelAnswer: Careful sharing helps protect your privacy and safety.
Public posts can reveal sensitive personal information that others may misuse.

written.text: Q11.13. What should you do if you receive an email from an unknown sender asking for personal information?
written.finalAnswer: Ignore or delete the email, and do not provide personal information or click its links.

rubric.why: Avoiding engagement is the safe response to an unknown request.
rubric.description: State what to do with the email.
rubric.how: Say to ignore or delete it.

rubric.why: The answer should avoid exposing information or following risky links.
rubric.how: Do not provide personal information or click links.

modelAnswer: Ignore or delete the email.
Do not provide personal information or click any links in it.

written.text: Q11.14. What is the purpose of privacy laws regarding your personal information?
written.finalAnswer: Privacy laws help protect personal information and set rules for how it may be collected, used, and shared.

rubric.why: Protection of personal information is the main purpose.
rubric.how: Mention protection of personal information or privacy.

rubric.why: The answer should describe how laws regulate data handling.
rubric.how: Mention rules about collecting, using, sharing, or accessing information.

modelAnswer: Privacy laws help protect your personal information.
They set rules for how it may be collected, used, and shared.

written.text: Q11.15. How do privacy laws protect you from unauthorized access to your data?
written.finalAnswer: Privacy laws require safeguards and regulate access and use of personal data, helping prevent unauthorized access or disclosure.

rubric.why: Safeguards help reduce the chance of unauthorized access.
rubric.how: State that laws require or support safeguards to protect data.

rubric.why: The answer should connect rules to controlling access or disclosure.
rubric.how: Mention regulating access, use, or disclosure of data.

modelAnswer: Privacy laws require safeguards and set rules for handling personal data.
These rules help prevent unauthorized access to or disclosure of your data.

written.text: Q11.16. What is the difference between copyright, trademarks, and patents?
written.finalAnswer: Copyright protects creative works, trademarks identify brands or goods, and patents protect inventions.

rubric.why: Copyright must be distinguished by the type of work it protects.
rubric.how: Say it protects creative works.

rubric.why: The other two forms must be distinguished by their purpose.
rubric.how: State that trademarks identify brands and patents protect inventions.

modelAnswer: Copyright protects creative works, while trademarks identify brands or goods.
Patents protect inventions.

written.text: Q11.17. Why is it important to respect intellectual property rights?
written.finalAnswer: Respecting intellectual property rights recognizes creators’ ownership, supports their work, and helps avoid legal consequences.

rubric.why: Respect begins by recognizing the creator’s ownership and rights.
rubric.how: Mention respecting creators and their ownership.

rubric.why: Respect also supports lawful use and prevents consequences.
rubric.how: Mention supporting creators or avoiding legal consequences.

modelAnswer: Respecting intellectual property recognizes creators’ ownership and rights.
It supports their work and helps users avoid legal consequences.

written.text: Q11.18. What is software piracy, and why is it harmful?
written.finalAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software; it harms creators and may lead to legal consequences.

rubric.why: The answer must define software piracy as illegal software use or copying.
rubric.how: Mention illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.

rubric.why: The answer should state a harm or consequence.
rubric.how: Mention harm to creators or possible legal consequences.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.
It harms creators and may lead to legal consequences.

written.text: Q11.19. How can you identify reliable sources when researching online?
written.finalAnswer: Compare information across multiple reputable sources, check the author’s credentials, and confirm that evidence supports the claims.

rubric.why: Cross-checking information helps reveal errors or bias.
rubric.description: Mention checking more than one reputable source.
rubric.how: Compare information across reliable sources.

rubric.why: Checking expertise and evidence helps judge credibility.
rubric.how: Check author credentials or supporting evidence.

modelAnswer: Compare the information with multiple reputable sources.
Check the author’s credentials and whether evidence supports the claims.

written.text: Q11.20. What is one way to protect your privacy during online research?
written.finalAnswer: Avoid entering unnecessary personal information on websites while researching online.

rubric.why: The response must give a practical privacy action.
rubric.how: Say to avoid or limit sharing information.

rubric.why: The action must relate to protecting privacy during research.
rubric.description: Connect the action to online research.
rubric.how: Mention not entering unnecessary personal information on websites.

modelAnswer: Avoid entering unnecessary personal information on websites.
Share only the information needed for your online research.

written.text: Q11.21. What are some signs that you might be developing an internet addiction?
written.finalAnswer: Signs may include losing control of time online, neglecting school or other responsibilities, and continuing internet use despite harmful effects.

rubric.why: Difficulty controlling use is a warning sign.
rubric.description: Name a sign related to time or control.
rubric.how: Mention spending excessive time online or difficulty stopping.

rubric.why: The answer should include an effect on daily life or wellbeing.
rubric.description: Name a further sign or effect.
rubric.how: Mention neglected responsibilities or harmful effects on daily life.

modelAnswer: Signs include spending excessive time online or finding it difficult to stop.
You may neglect school, responsibilities, sleep, or relationships despite harmful effects.

written.text: Q11.1. 1. Discuss the importance of responsible computer usage in today's digital world. Explain how selecting the right hardware and software can affect safety, efficiency, and compatibility in computer use.
written.finalAnswer: Responsible use protects users and information, and suitable hardware and software improve safety, efficiency, and compatibility.

rubric.why: The response must explain the purpose and value of responsible use.
rubric.how: Explain that it protects users, information, or devices and supports wise choices.

rubric.why: Compatibility depends on matching requirements to the computer.
rubric.how: Describe checking requirements and matching them with specifications.

rubric.why: Safety is a required effect of selecting and using technology responsibly.
rubric.how: Include a relevant safety practice such as trusted software, updates, antivirus, or account protection.

rubric.why: The question also asks how choices affect efficiency and use.
rubric.description: Discuss efficiency and finish with the overall benefit.
rubric.how: Explain how suitable, compatible choices help devices perform tasks effectively.

modelAnswer: Responsible computer usage is important because computers and digital platforms are part of everyday life.
Users should protect personal information, use devices carefully, and make wise choices about hardware and software.
Choose equipment and programs that meet your needs and obtain software from trusted sources.
Check the software system requirements and match them with the computer’s specifications.
Compatible hardware and software work together and help avoid errors or performance problems.
Suitable choices help a computer perform tasks efficiently.
Safe practices include using antivirus software, installing updates, and protecting accounts with strong, unique passwords.
Therefore, responsible use improves safety, efficiency, and compatibility.

written.text: Q11.2. Describe the steps you should take to ensure the safe operation of digital platforms and devices.
written.finalAnswer: Use trusted software and updates, antivirus protection, strong unique passwords and 2FA, cautious browsing, privacy settings, and careful account and network practices.

rubric.why: Safe devices need trustworthy software and protection against threats.
rubric.how: Mention trusted software, updates, or antivirus.

rubric.why: Account security is an important part of safe platform use.
rubric.how: Include strong unique passwords and 2FA.

rubric.why: Users must avoid common online risks.
rubric.description: Describe safe browsing and network choices.
rubric.how: Mention avoiding suspicious links/downloads or sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi.

rubric.why: Careful sharing and monitoring help maintain privacy and security.
rubric.how: Mention privacy settings, careful sharing, or reviewing activity.

modelAnswer: Keep the device and software updated, and use antivirus software.
Install software from trusted sources and check that it is compatible with the device.
Use strong, unique passwords and enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA).
Do not click unknown links or download files from untrusted sources.
Be cautious of emails or messages asking for personal information; verify them before responding.
Avoid sensitive transactions on public Wi-Fi because these networks are often less secure.
Use privacy settings and do not publicly share sensitive personal information.
Review account activity regularly and report or address anything unusual.

written.text: Q11.3. Explain the concept of data ethics and its importance in handling personal and sensitive information. Discuss the principles of transparency, respect for privacy, and accountability.
written.finalAnswer: Data ethics means handling data responsibly through transparency, respect for privacy, and accountability, protecting people’s personal and sensitive information.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the overall idea of data ethics.
rubric.how: Describe it as responsible or ethical handling of data.

rubric.why: Transparency is one of the principles specifically requested.
rubric.how: Say data practices should be open and clearly explained.

rubric.why: Respect for privacy protects people’s information and choices.
rubric.how: Explain that personal and sensitive data should be protected and handled respectfully.

rubric.why: Accountability ensures that data handlers answer for their actions.
rubric.how: Mention responsibility for secure and proper data use.

modelAnswer: Data ethics is the responsible and fair handling of data, especially personal and sensitive information.
It matters because careless data use can expose information or harm the people it concerns.
Transparency means being open and clear about what data is collected and how it is used.
People should be able to understand the purpose of data collection and use.
Respect for privacy means protecting personal information and not using or sharing it carelessly.
Data should be handled in ways that respect people’s rights and privacy.
Accountability means that people or organizations handling data are responsible for their actions.
These principles build trust and help prevent misuse or unauthorized disclosure of data.

written.text: Q11.4. Analyze the impact of privacy laws on protecting personal information in the digital age. How do laws like the Personal Data Protection Bill in Pakistan help safeguard user data?
written.finalAnswer: Privacy laws set rules and safeguards for collecting, using, storing, and sharing personal data, helping protect users from misuse and unauthorized access.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the purpose of privacy laws in the digital age.
rubric.description: Explain the role of privacy laws.
rubric.how: State that they protect personal information in digital settings.

rubric.why: Laws affect how organizations handle data.
rubric.how: Mention regulating collection, use, storage, or sharing.

rubric.why: The question asks how such laws safeguard user data.
rubric.how: Connect safeguards to preventing unauthorized access, misuse, or disclosure.

rubric.why: The response must relate the example law to user protection and responsibility.
rubric.description: Apply the explanation to Pakistan’s bill.
rubric.how: Explain that the bill is intended to support responsible handling and protection of users’ data.

modelAnswer: Privacy laws are important because people share personal information through digital services every day.
These laws set rules for how personal data may be collected, used, stored, and shared.
They encourage organizations to handle user information responsibly and put safeguards in place.
Safeguards can reduce unauthorized access, misuse, or disclosure of data.
Privacy laws also support individuals’ privacy and help clarify responsibilities for data handlers.
The Personal Data Protection Bill in Pakistan is intended to provide a framework for protecting personal data.
Such a framework can guide organizations in handling user data more carefully and securely.
Therefore, privacy laws help users by setting responsibilities and reducing risks to their personal information.

written.text: Q11.5. Discuss the different types of intellectual property rights, including copyright, trademarks, and patents.
written.finalAnswer: Copyright protects creative works, trademarks distinguish brands or goods, and patents protect inventions.

rubric.why: The answer must identify what copyright protects.
rubric.how: State that copyright protects creative works.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish trademarks from other rights.
rubric.how: State that trademarks identify or distinguish brands or goods.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the subject protected by a patent.
rubric.how: State that patents protect inventions.

rubric.why: The response should connect the types to protection of creators and owners.
rubric.description: Summarize the purpose of these rights.
rubric.how: Explain that these rights protect ownership and distinguish different kinds of intellectual property.

modelAnswer: Intellectual property rights protect creations and ideas belonging to their owners.
Copyright protects creative works, such as written, artistic, or other original material.
It helps protect the creator’s rights over the work.
Trademarks are names, signs, or symbols that identify and distinguish a brand or goods.
They help people recognize the source of a product or service.
Patents protect inventions and give the inventor legal rights over the invention.
Copyright, trademarks, and patents apply to different kinds of intellectual property.
Respecting these rights means using protected material or inventions only as permitted.

written.text: Q11.6. Describe the ethical and legal responsibilities related to intellectual property rights. What are the consequences of violating these rights, such as through software piracy or unauthorized use of copyrighted material?
written.finalAnswer: Users should respect ownership, obtain permission or licences, and avoid piracy; violations can harm creators and lead to legal consequences.

rubric.why: The answer must identify the ethical duty to respect owners’ rights.
rubric.how: Mention respecting creators’ ownership and intellectual property.

rubric.why: Users must obtain lawful permission for protected material.
rubric.description: State how to use protected material lawfully.
rubric.how: Mention permission, a licence, or authorized use.

rubric.why: The question gives piracy and unauthorized use as examples of violations.
rubric.how: Explain that piracy or use without authorization violates rights.

rubric.why: Consequences of violation are expressly required.
rubric.how: Mention harm to creators and possible legal consequences or penalties.

modelAnswer: Users have an ethical and legal responsibility to respect the intellectual property rights of creators and owners.
They should obtain permission or a licence before using protected material when required.
Software piracy is the illegal copying, distribution, or use of software.
Copying or distributing copyrighted material without authorization also violates the owner’s rights.
These actions can deprive creators of recognition or payment and harm their work.
Unauthorized use may also lead to legal consequences or penalties.
Users should obtain software and other material from legitimate sources.
Respecting intellectual property supports creators and keeps computer use lawful and responsible.

written.text: Q11.7. Outline effective techniques for conducting safe and credible online research. How can users evaluate the reliability of sources and avoid privacy risks during their research?
written.finalAnswer: Use multiple reputable sources, check authors’ credentials and evidence, and protect privacy by avoiding unnecessary sharing of personal information.

rubric.why: Reliable research uses and compares reputable sources.
rubric.how: Mention using more than one reputable source.

rubric.why: A source’s expertise and supporting evidence help evaluate reliability.
rubric.description: Explain how to evaluate a source.
rubric.how: Check authorship, credentials, evidence, and whether claims are supported.

rubric.why: The question requires ways to avoid privacy risks.
rubric.how: Avoid entering or sharing unnecessary personal information.

rubric.why: Safe research also involves avoiding online threats.
rubric.how: Avoid suspicious links or downloads and use careful browsing practices.

modelAnswer: Begin research with reputable sources and compare information across more than one source.
Check the author’s credentials and the date or relevance of the information.
Look for evidence that supports the claims and notice whether the source is balanced and trustworthy.
Do not accept information only because a website is popular or attractive.
Avoid clicking unknown links or downloading files from untrusted sources.
Do not enter or share unnecessary personal information while researching.
Use privacy settings and be cautious about forms that ask for personal details.
These steps help make online research safer and its information more credible.

written.text: Q11.8. Discuss the concept of internet addiction and its potential impact on individuals. How can recognizing the signs of addiction, setting time limits, and finding offline activities help promote balanced internet usage?
written.finalAnswer: Internet addiction involves excessive, difficult-to-control use that affects daily life; recognizing signs, setting time limits, and choosing offline activities support balance.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the concept of internet addiction.
rubric.how: Describe excessive or difficult-to-control internet use.

rubric.why: The impact on individuals must be discussed.
rubric.how: Mention effects on responsibilities, school, sleep, health, or relationships.

rubric.why: Recognizing signs and limiting use are specified in the question.
rubric.how: Mention identifying signs and setting time limits.

rubric.why: Offline activities can help restore balance.
rubric.description: Explain the role of offline activities.
rubric.how: Give examples of offline activities and connect them to balanced use.

modelAnswer: Internet addiction is excessive internet use that becomes difficult to control.
It may interfere with schoolwork, sleep, responsibilities, health, and relationships.
Signs can include spending more time online than intended or continuing despite harmful effects.
Recognizing these signs is the first step toward balanced use.
Setting daily time limits and taking breaks can help control time online.
A person can plan when to use the internet and keep time for other responsibilities.
Offline activities such as exercise, reading, hobbies, or meeting people provide healthy alternatives.
These steps can support a balanced and responsible use of the internet.

examTips: Short questions usually require a clear definition, a reason, or two practical safety measures; answer directly and include the key terms.
Long questions often use command words such as discuss, describe, explain, or analyze. Organize the response into clear points and address every part of the prompt.
Marks are earned for accurate points, explanations, and relevant examples—not by repeating the question.
For data and privacy questions, use terms such as personal information, privacy, transparency, accountability, safeguards, and unauthorized access.
For intellectual property questions, clearly distinguish copyright (creative works), trademarks (brands or goods), and patents (inventions).

hints: Think of what responsible use protects.

yourTurn.question: Q11.1. What is the importance of using computers safely and responsibly?
solution: Using computers safely and responsibly protects personal information.
It helps prevent harm and supports wise choices when using computers.
yourTurn.answer: It protects personal information, helps prevent harm, and supports wise, responsible choices when using computers.

hints: Think about the extra thing needed after a password.

yourTurn.question: Q11.9. What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA), and why is it useful?
solution: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) requires a second form of verification in addition to a password.
It adds an extra layer of security to help protect an account.
yourTurn.answer: 2FA requires a second form of verification as well as a password, adding an extra layer of account security.

example.question: Q11.1. 1. Discuss the importance of responsible computer usage in today's digital world. Explain how selecting the right hardware and software can affect safety, efficiency, and compatibility in computer use.
example.answer:
Responsible computer usage is important because computers and digital platforms are part of everyday life.
Users should protect personal information, use devices carefully, and make wise choices about hardware and software.
Choose equipment and programs that meet your needs and obtain software from trusted sources.
Check the software system requirements and match them with the computer’s specifications.
Compatible hardware and software work together and help avoid errors or performance problems.
Suitable choices help a computer perform tasks efficiently.
Safe practices include using antivirus software, installing updates, and protecting accounts with strong, unique passwords.
Therefore, responsible use improves safety, efficiency, and compatibility.

explain.title: Use computers responsibly
explain.body: Responsible use means protecting your personal information, making thoughtful choices, and considering how your actions affect yourself and others.

explain.title: Choose compatible technology
explain.body: Choose hardware and software that meet your needs. Check software system requirements and compare them with your computer’s specifications so the parts work together.

explain.title: Secure devices and accounts
explain.body: Use antivirus software and regular updates. Create strong, unique passwords, enable two-factor authentication, avoid unknown links and untrusted downloads, and be cautious with public Wi-Fi.

explain.title: Protect privacy and handle data ethically
explain.body: Think before sharing information online and use privacy settings. Data ethics calls for transparency, respect for privacy, and accountability when handling personal or sensitive information.

explain.title: Respect rights and research carefully
explain.body: Copyright protects creative works, trademarks identify brands or goods, and patents protect inventions. Avoid software piracy; check multiple reputable sources and the author’s credentials before trusting online information.

mistakes: Do not share passwords or use the same password for every account; use strong, unique passwords and 2FA.
Do not assume that a public Wi-Fi network is safe for sensitive transactions.
Do not click unknown links or provide personal information to an unknown email sender.
Do not treat a website’s popularity or attractive design as proof that its information is reliable.
Do not confuse copyright, trademarks, and patents: they protect different things.
Do not copy, distribute, or use software illegally; software piracy violates intellectual property rights.
When answering a long question, address every part of the prompt instead of giving only a definition.
